paper.title: TinyRank: Compact Document Classification with Dual Routing

research_question: Whether combining a global router and local context gate improves document classification without high computational cost.
method_chain: global router G and token gate C

claims.claim: TinyRank improves macro-F1 by 8 percentage points over StrongBase on both datasets.

evidence.observation: Dataset A is 0.78 versus 0.70, an 0.08 difference; Dataset B is 0.78 versus 0.74, an 0.04 difference.

claims.boundary: The reported single run shows an 8-point gain on Dataset A and a 4-point gain on Dataset B, not 8 points on both.
risks: Headline arithmetic is wrong for Dataset B.
Only one run per model is reported.

claims.claim: Both G and C are essential to TinyRank's gain.

evidence.observation: Full TinyRank and the variant without C both report 0.78 macro-F1; removing G reports 0.76.

claims.boundary: The one-run Dataset A ablation shows a 2-point decrease without G but no observed decrease without C; necessity of C is not demonstrated.
risks: The prose directly contradicts the table for C.
Ablation is limited to Dataset A and one run.

evidence.observation: The paper reports separate within-dataset results on one technical-support dataset and one product-review dataset.

claims.boundary: TinyRank outperforms the selected baselines in one reported run within each of two datasets; cross-domain transfer is not tested.
risks: No cross-domain train-test transfer is reported.
No uncertainty or repeated runs are reported.

claims.claim: TinyRank is broadly robust to noisy real-world text.

evidence.observation: With 10% random token deletion on Dataset A, TinyRank reports 0.71 macro-F1 and StrongBase 0.65.

claims.boundary: The reported run supports better performance than StrongBase under one synthetic corruption level on Dataset A only.
risks: Only one corruption type, level, dataset, and run are evaluated.

evidence.observation: The only compute information is that training completed on a single unspecified GPU.

claims.boundary: No compute-efficiency conclusion is defensible without hardware, time, memory, parameter, energy, or compute-matched comparison data.
risks: Decisive efficiency measurements are not specified in the paper.

claims.claim: TinyRank exceeds StrongBase in the reported main-result runs.

evidence.observation: TinyRank reports 0.78 versus 0.70 on Dataset A and 0.78 versus 0.74 on Dataset B.

claims.boundary: This describes the displayed single-run results only and does not establish stability or unbiased generalization.
risks: The best checkpoint is selected using test macro-F1.
No repeated-run uncertainty or statistical test is reported.

consistency_issues.description: The prose claims an 8-point gain on both datasets, but Table 1 shows only a 4-point gain on Dataset B.
consistency_issues.impact: A headline quantitative contribution is false for one of two datasets.

consistency_issues.description: The prose says removing either module damages performance, while the without-C row equals the full model at 0.78.
consistency_issues.impact: The only ablation directly contradicts necessity of C.

consistency_issues.description: The checkpoint is selected using the test metric and no validation procedure is reported.
consistency_issues.impact: Reported test performance may be optimistically selected.

unknowns.item: Random seed, batch size, validation procedure, stopping rule, encoder identity, exact split counts, baseline tuning details, statistical tests, and detailed compute measurements.
unknowns.impact: Reproducibility, uncertainty, leakage risk, and efficiency cannot be fully assessed.

unknowns.item: Field-wide novelty of the dual-routing architecture.
Stability of the reported gains and the contribution of Module C across datasets and seeds.
unknowns.impact: Single-run internal evidence cannot establish stability or module necessity.

next_checks: Recalculate every headline gain from Table 1 and reconcile the Dataset B discrepancy.
Recheck Table 2 and repeat the C ablation across seeds and Dataset B.
Use a validation set or nested model-selection procedure instead of selecting on test macro-F1.
Test cross-domain transfer rather than separate within-dataset performance.
Measure compute against a matched baseline with specified hardware and resource metrics.
